cohort: 65 women aged 16 to 45 years, either diagnosed with polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) or without PCOS.
finding: The study found that women with PCOS had a significantly higher incidence of maternal complications during pregnancy, including gestational diabetes and pregnancy-induced hypertension, as well as adverse fetal and neonatal outcomes such as preterm deliveries, low birth weight, intrauterine growth restriction, multifetal pregnancies, early labor, and losses.
